what_matters.head: Wall Street's AI stocks sold off hard: the S&P 500 fund fell 4.4%, about 6.6 times its usual daily move, and the chip fund 12.2%.
what_matters.detail: The Nasdaq 100 fund fell 6.5%. CNBC said the Nasdaq had its worst day since April 2025, and Yahoo Finance said the Dow fell more than 1,800 points, or 3.4%. CNBC tied it to fears that the AI build-out will slow after Tuesday's Democratic sweep: the states with the biggest data-centre plans voted Democratic, and voters sided against data centres in 40 of 41 local ballot measures. On Wednesday night Meta's Dina Powell McCormick said building data centres is 'going to be harder' after the elections. Qualcomm's weak forecast for this quarter added to the fall. Nomura's Charlie McElligott wrote that the main trigger was not a sudden turn for the worse in the businesses, and Yahoo Finance said hedge funds were locking in this year's gains. Nvidia lost almost $450 billion in market value (CNBC).

what_matters.head: The sell-off spread to Asia this morning: Japan's Nikkei fell 7% at the open, and Korea's and Taiwan's main indexes more than 8%.
what_matters.detail: Reuters said TSMC fell as much as 8.5% in Taipei, and put Samsung down nearly 10% and SK Hynix 12% in Seoul; at 12:05 SGT they were down 5.8% and 8.3%. In Reuters' latest update Nasdaq futures were up 1.4%. The futures move is not in Thursday's US prices.

what_matters.head: OCBC's Q3 profit rose 3% from a year earlier to S$2.04B, a touch above the S$2.0B Bloomberg's estimate expected.
what_matters.detail: Net interest income rose 4% to S$2.31B, and the margin narrowed 18 basis points (MT Newswires; the article read gives no level). Other income fell 10% to S$1.42B, mainly on weaker results at insurer Great Eastern. Customer loans rose 14% to S$372B. The chief executive said conditions remain uncertain. DBS's Q3 profit missed analysts' figures yesterday. By 12:05 SGT OCBC was down 0.5%.

after_data.text: Bloomberg reported on 5 Nov, citing people familiar with the matter, that Micron has all but halted work on a planned chip plant in Taoyuan, Taiwan, budgeted at $3–4.5B and due to open in 2028, amid its pay dispute with the local union. In a statement Micron said it was confident of keeping business running for its customers, without addressing the plant (TheStreet). The report's time is not given, so it may or may not be in Thursday's US prices.

latest.tape_note: On Thursday the S&P 500 fund fell 4.4%, the Nasdaq 100 fund 6.5% and the chip fund 12.2%. VIX rose 70% to 28.2, about 10 times its usual daily move. The 10-year yield fell 6 basis points to 4.84%. The dollar index rose 0.2%. US crude rose 4.3% to $91.88 a barrel, and gold slipped 0.5%. The US dollar was flat against the Singapore dollar.
latest.tonight: The US jobs report for October is out at 21:30 SGT. Micron's third round of talks with its Taoyuan union was set tentatively for today.

recent.headline: Wall Street's AI stocks sold off hard: the S&P 500 fund fell 4.4%, about 6.6 times its usual daily move, and the chip fund 12.2%.
Wall Street rose after the Democratic sweep, led by Microsoft and Amazon, while chip and data-centre stocks fell.
The AP projects that Democrats win both the House and the Senate, and US stock futures and Asian chip stocks fell on it.
Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal, and Lumentum fell 18.6%, about 3.4 times its usual daily move.
Intel fell 28.6% on Friday, about 7.5 times its usual daily move, and the chip fund fell 8.2%, about 3.5 times usual.
